Why it matters
Habitat destruction: animals lose their homes and food when trees are cut down.
Soil erosion: without tree roots, rain washes the soil away.
Disrupted food chains: when species lose their food, others struggle.
Loss of pollinators: forests find it harder to grow back.

INNOVATION PROJECT
Our problem: DEFORESTATION  · WISE Academy · Orlando, Florida · FIRST LEGO League Challenge · BIOGLOW 2026–27
3 · CREATE
OUR SOLUTION:name · Mahdi + Ammar decide
When a tree has to come down, plant two new trees for every one, before the cutting starts. Where you can, cut it only halfway and leave the trunk standing, so animals still have a home while the new trees grow.
Our solution, drawn and labelledArrows point at each part
Glue the drawing here
15.8 × 13 in
How it works · 1 · Before cutting
Plant two new trees for every tree that has to come down.
Companies that cut trees for wood and houses carry seeds and plant new ones every time they cut.
Mahdi
How it works · 2 · When cutting
Where you can, cut it only halfway and leave the trunk standing.
How it works · 3 · While they grow
Animals still have a home in the trunk while the new trees grow.
What already exists → What we made, and what is new
What already exists
What we made, and what is new
People plant trees back after they cut.
→
Two new trees for every one, planted before the cutting starts.
People protest and ask builders to stop.
→
Something hands-on: if you cut a tree, you plant more.
Whole trees are cut down.
→
Cut only halfway. The trunk left standing is still a home for animals. Cutting half is a new idea our whole team discussed.
